title: Welcome to the Adaptive Palette.
adapts: This palette makes use of AI to adapt to your personal information, your contexts and your needs.
privacy: The AI runs on your own computer, and your messages are never sent to the cloud.
overview: The Adaptive Palette allows Bliss symbol users to use many Bliss strategies when composing a message, and enhances the message through both word suggestions and sentence suggestions.
benefit-1: These components have the potential to provide users with: access to vocabulary that is not available in the programmed vocabulary set,
benefit-2: increased accuracy of the communication message,
benefit-3: and increased speed in communicating a message.
pictures: The Adaptive Palette supports AAC users who communicate using Bliss symbols. While the current palette displays Bliss symbols, the cells in the palette can be populated with any type of picture.
folders: In the default grid, symbols are grouped by topic, but users who take part in testing will have their own vocabulary and layout. A cell representing a vocabulary group, such as food, has a fold in the top right corner.
food: If you select a symbol such as food, it opens to a page with food related vocabulary.
vocabulary: The vocabulary takes up most of the palette space. Let's take a look at the other parts of the palette, starting at the top.
top-row: The top row has the Add Symbol to Message button, the Adjust Settings button and the About Me button. These are described in a separate video.
message: Under this row is the message window.
message-insert: When you click on a vocabulary item, both the symbol and the word it represents are inserted into the message window. Notice that the food items do not have a fold in the top right corner. When I click on one of these symbols, it is inserted into the message window, along with its word.
back-home: To the left of the message window are the back button, which takes you back to the previous page of the palette, and the home button, which takes you back to the top level of vocabulary.
speak: To the right of the message window are two buttons. On the far right is the speak button, which speaks the content of the message window. The button right beside the message window, the make sentence button, is one of the AI features, and is described in a separate video.
predictions: The row of green cells underneath the message window fills with words that are predicted to be useful next words, based on your message. This word suggestion feature is explained in a separate video.
edit-row: The row of cells under the word prediction cells lets you edit the message in the message window, by removing words added by mistake, or by using Bliss symbol strategies.
cursor: The forward and backward cells move the cursor forward or backward in the message window.
constructed: I have constructed the message: want hamburger bun. To make the message more complete, I will add the word I at the beginning, and then add the word in, between hamburger and bun.
backward: Let's move the cursor from the end of the message to the beginning, using the backward button.
add-i: Now I'll add the word I.
forward: Then move the cursor to the right of the word hamburger,
delete: The delete button removes the word to the left of the cursor from the message window.
delete-all: The delete all button removes all words in the message window.
closing-users: Now that you are familiar with the layout of the Adaptive Palette, refer to the following videos to learn how to use the other functions of the palette. For AAC users: About Me. Constructing a Message. Word Suggestions. Sentence Suggestions, including Bliss Strategies. Message Attributes. Create New Bliss Words. Blissymbol Indicators and Modifiers. Using switch access.
closing-support: For AAC support people: Installing the Desktop Version, and first run setup. Settings Overview. About Me. Setting Up Switch Access and Shortcut Keys. Changing the language.
